about: > Half Life is a permanent state of change. Nothing holds its shape for long. Time moves, places shift, people become someone else, and so do you. You are still conscious, still moving, still wanting, and the only way through is to move with it.

posts.title: Entry 000001
posts.body:
Hello,

For some considerable time I have entertained the notion that I ought to have a website. The reasons for this conviction remain somewhat obscure, but the conviction itself has proved remarkably durable. At last, through a combination of industry, vanity, and an unexpected abundance of free time, the thing now exists.

My present scheme is to begin with several long and shamelessly retrospective accounts of the year thus far: projects undertaken with varying degrees of competence, places visited, objects made, and other episodes which, through the generous distortions of memory, now seem worthy of documentation.

Whether any of this will prove useful to anyone is doubtful. Fortunately, usefulness was never among the requirements.

Once I have exhausted accounts of the recent past, I shall concern myself with the future.

bestiary.name: Rainbow Trout
bestiary.lore:
The demon of Pine Lake. The old anglers say it was a drowned spirit before it was a fish, and that the red band along its side is a wound that never closed.

It keeps to the cold, dark water where the light gives out, and rises only at dusk to take whatever touches the surface. Those who have hooked it speak of a pull like the lake itself dragging the line down.

When it leaps, it is not trying to escape. It is looking at whoever dared.

bestiary.name: Sunfish
bestiary.lore: A round-bodied panfish of warm, weedy shallows. Small, but bold enough to charge anything that drifts near its nest.

bestiary.name: Crappie
bestiary.lore: A speckled, deep-bodied fish that schools around sunken brush and feeds most at dawn and dusk. Anglers call it papermouth, for a lip so thin a hook can tear free.

bestiary.name: Bass
bestiary.lore: An ambush hunter that holds beside cover and takes its prey in one gulp. It is the fish most lake anglers are really after.
